approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph genetic algorithm whose evaluation budget is allocated by a task-local Gaussian process. It keeps every accepted molecule of the current objective session in an archive and a bounded population of the 64 best, samples breeding parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds a fresh surplus pool of sixteen candidates per announced member by connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing mutation or by successive local graph edits from seven atom/bond/ring operator families, with direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange disabled. Stable canonical identity and duplicate rejection govern pool admission, and a narrow sulfur-environment rule rejects any offspring that introduces a new outside-envelope sulfur local environment relative to its own scored generating parents, after which the inherited bounded refill loop continues. A Gaussian process on integer-count Morgan fingerprints with a generalized count Tanimoto kernel is refitted to all accepted scores before every announced batch, normalized by the running score mean and population standard deviation. The ten molecules actually evaluated are chosen by correlated posterior sampling: one joint draw across the whole pool, scaled by the archive score spread and added to the fitted posterior means, then ten sequential masked arg-max picks with first-index ties. Nothing in the Parent depends on whether the search is currently making progress.
approach.novelty: This Child makes the allocator sharpen itself exactly while the search has stopped improving. It adds the same stagnation counter the previous round's arms bound - one integer count of consecutive announced batches that did not raise this session's own best score, triggering at three and resetting on the first improving batch - and, while that trigger is active, multiplies only the sampled residual term of the allocation draw by a single preregistered factor of two thirds, restoring the inherited amplitude as soon as the session improves again. The posterior means, kernel, normalization, noise, covariance factorization, the one random draw with its shape and order, the candidate pool and the masked tie rule are all left exactly as the Parent computes them, so the only thing that changes is how far a sampled deviation can carry a choice away from the model's own ranking during stagnation. This is the opposite direction of the one dose ever tried on this channel: the sibling that widened the same term by half during the same trigger reliably moved picks into the uncertain tail and lost, and its same-pool audit measured why - the molecules it swapped in were far worse than the ones it displaced. Contraction is untested, and the Parent's own stalled stream says where its gains actually live: in the top few percent of the fitted mean, never in the uncertain tail. The round's other arms change different things - one perturbs the random path alone with no law change, one restricts which candidates are eligible, one combines two already measured generator and breadth settings - so no sibling tests the amplitude of the sampled deviation downward. Earlier arms on this channel either rescaled it for the whole run or deleted it entirely; both lost, which is why the dose here stays interior and nothing about the correlated structure is removed.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-1744a1494180 is complete on the current panel: three ok replicas, 15 of 15 cells, macro mean 0.596453 with population SD 0.033970, seed macros 0.643098 / 0.563173 / 0.583088, and only +0.000783 over its own Parent n-62daf219c70a. The behaviour that limits it is how its correlated Thompson allocator spends evaluations once the session has measurably stopped improving: at the inherited residual amplitude the sampled draws keep moving the ten masked argmax choices off the top of the fitted posterior mean and into the model's uncertain tail, which in this regime is where this Anchor's own evaluations produce nothing. Recomputed read-only from its published receipts (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0|1|2/trajectories/<task>.jsonl and the matching per-task candidate logs), 91 of its 435 announced batches are allocated with the consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter at or above three, in 29 episodes across 13 of 15 sessions, with deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never triggering; that is 910 of its 4,350 evaluated offspring, and this recomputation reproduces the published round-38 figures for the same Anchor exactly. Those 910 picks average 0.4046, beat their best generating parent 8.6% of the time, produce 28 sequential incumbent increments summing 0.476561, and carry positive child-minus-best-parent mass 1.6436. Split by the same fitted posterior the allocator itself used: the 233 picks in the top 3% of pool posterior mean supply 18 of the 28 incumbent increments, 0.9353 of the positive gain mass and a 16.7% parent-beating rate; the 64 picks below the median posterior mean average 0.1985 with zero incumbent increments; the 43 picks in the top posterior-SD decile average 0.0906 with zero parent beats and zero incumbent increments; 22 of the 910 are molecules of at most four heavy atoms. The increase direction on this exact channel is refuted twice and the refutation located the cause: whole-run error-calibrated rescaling lost 0.038141 (n-38bcd7569cce) and the stall-gated factor 1.5 lost 0.009718 (n-189cd716f027) with all three seed macros lower, its widened draws swapping in 43 molecules averaging 0.182 against 0.363 for the 43 displaced Anchor picks on identical first-stall pools. The channel cannot be deleted either: removing the sampled residual costs 0.116317 (n-f04cec6ab705), removing cross-candidate correlation 0.050545 (n-8df0bb3bbcfe) and removing the composite selector 0.128183 (n-605c7a785b51). The untested direction is interior contraction, which Curate registers as the open question h-a63b8fa90bc39b03 on this mechanism identity.

adoptions.applicability: The adopted condition is available unchanged here because this campaign's trigger already uses the paper's own success definition at the paper's own default of three, and the Anchor's stalled-regime evidence independently says the uncertain tail is where its evaluations fail. The sharpening is realized on sampling amplitude rather than on a region side length because this allocator samples a fitted posterior over a finite fresh pool of molecular graphs and has no coordinate box to shrink.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Failure-counter-conditioned sharpening: a failure is an announced batch that produces no improvement on the incumbent best, a bound number of consecutive failures triggers a contraction of the region the sampler is effectively allowed to roam, and the condition is released as soon as the search improves again.

deviations.adopted_setting: The sampled residual amplitude is multiplied by 0.6666666666666666 while the counter is at or above three, and the counter is reset only by an improving batch.
deviations.paper_setting: After tau_fail consecutive failures the trust-region side length is halved, a factor of 0.5 on the region extent, and the counters are reset when the size changes.
deviations.reason: Full removal of this residual is already measured at -0.116317 on this Anchor, so the dose must stay strictly interior, and the ticket binds a factor strictly between 0.5 and 1.0. Two thirds is the reciprocal of the single measured dose on this exact channel (1.5, -0.009718), which makes the directional contrast dose-matched rather than confounded by step size: on the 13 exact same-state first stalled batches it moves 54 of 130 positions against that arm's 56, and 38 swapped molecules against its 43, while realizing less than half the pick displacement of full removal (120 of 130).

deviations.adopted_setting: One fixed threshold K=3 for contraction only; no doubling branch and no success counter.
deviations.paper_setting: tau_fail = ceil(d/q) from the problem dimension and batch size, with tau_succ = 3 doubling the region after consecutive successes.
deviations.reason: The threshold is frozen by the ticket to the value the four round-38 siblings bound, so this position differs from them in one element only, and there is no dimension d or continuous region whose growth could be scheduled. Widening the same term during stalls is the refuted direction here, so no expansion branch is implemented.

deviations.adopted_setting: The inherited fresh offspring pool, its generation routes, its size and the sequential masked arg-max selection are untouched, and nothing is ever discarded or restarted.
deviations.paper_setting: Candidates are min{100d, 5000} scrambled Sobol points regenerated per batch inside the trust region, each coordinate perturbed with probability min{1, 20/d}, and the region is discarded and reinitialized below L_min.
deviations.reason: Candidate construction, pool breadth and restarts are separate mechanisms in this campaign and have their own measured results (fresh-pool breadth and a stall-only mask restriction are other positions, and a population restart would discard the accepted archive this Anchor's positive components depend on). Keeping them fixed is what makes this an attributable single-element change.

adoptions.implementation_change: CONFIG gains stall_residual_schedule = {threshold_batches: 3, stalled_residual_factor: 0.6666666666666666}; Evolution keeps one integer counter of consecutive announced batches whose accepted maximum did not exceed the session best held at announcement, and while that counter is at or above three FingerprintPosterior.select computes samples = mean + (score_scale * residual_factor) * (normals @ Cholesky_factor.T) instead of mean + score_scale * (normals @ Cholesky_factor.T), restoring the inherited expression on the first improving batch.

literature_review.conclusion: Reused from the ticket's frozen Search Policy review and re-verified against the cited full text during planning: TuRBO conditions a sharpening response on a counter of consecutive batches without a new best, which is exactly the trigger this lineage already binds at K=3, and it attributes global Bayesian optimization's failure to overemphasized exploration from a global acquisition. That is the one element adopted, implemented as a single interior multiplicative contraction of the sampled residual during measured stagnation. The trust-region geometry, Sobol candidate construction, coordinate-sparse perturbation, region doubling and restart rules are refused, and the paper's own results are not evidence for this benchmark. The dose and the direction come from this campaign's own records: the increase direction is refuted twice on this channel with a measured cause, removal is strongly negative, and the Anchor's stalled stream places its realized gains at the top of the fitted mean and none in the uncertain tail. No framing source is mapped to this position, and no new asset or dependency is needed.

sources.applicability: The paper's diagnosis of 'an overemphasized exploration that results from global acquisition' is exactly what this Anchor's stalled stream shows: 18 of its 28 in-regime incumbent increments come from the top 3% of fitted posterior mean and none from the top posterior-SD decile, while the only widening dose ever tried there displaced better molecules. Only the principle transfers; the paper's continuous-space geometry, its scores and its benchmark results are not campaign evidence.
sources.finding: The paper attributes the failure of global Bayesian optimization in large spaces to 'the implicit homogeneity of the global probabilistic models' and to 'an overemphasized exploration that results from global acquisition', and answers it with local trust regions whose size is driven by success and failure counters and whose candidates are chosen by Thompson sampling.

This Anchor's bound trigger is the same failure definition at K=3; only the counter-conditioned sharpening response is adopted, realized here on the amplitude of the sampled residual, because this allocator has no trust-region box, no Sobol construction and no restart.
sources.finding: Exact elements: a success is a candidate that improves on the current best, otherwise the batch is a failure; after tau_succ consecutive successes 'we double the size of the TR' and after tau_fail consecutive failures 'we halve the size of the TR'; 'We reset the success and failure counters to zero after we change the size of the TR'; when the side length falls below L_min the trust region is discarded and a new one is initialized; candidates are min{100d, 5000} scrambled Sobol points inside the trust region, each coordinate perturbed with probability min{1, 20/d}; TuRBO-1 defaults tau_succ = 3, tau_fail = ceil(d/q), L_init = 0.8, L_min = 2^-7, L_max = 1.6.

hypothesis: Stall-conditioned contraction of the Thompson residual amplitude: while this session's counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches is at or above three, multiply only the sampled residual of the correlated fresh-pool allocation, score_scale * (standard_normals @ Cholesky_factor.T), by the fixed constant 0.6666666666666666 (the float64 nearest to 1/1.5, so sampled residual variance is four ninths of the inherited variance around unchanged count-GP posterior means), so the ten sequentially masked argmax choices of a stalled batch move toward higher fitted posterior mean and out of the high-posterior-SD tail. The factor is exactly 1.0 before the counter first reaches three and again from the batch after the first strictly improving batch. The fitted posterior mean, the count-Tanimoto kernel, normalization, noise, the covariance and its Cholesky factorization with the original jitter retries, the single standard-normal draw with its shape, order and consumption count, the sequential availability masks and the first-index tie rule are unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Sharper stall-time sampling picked better molecules and broke stalls sooner, but the panel slipped 0.0033, within path noise
finding_summary.insights: The stalled-regime allocation question now has a clear local answer. The two directions of the same knob behave as mirror images on identical pools: widening swapped in worse molecules and contraction swapped in better ones, so during stalls the model's predicted mean is a better guide than its uncertainty and, judged by the molecules it picks, the inherited amplitude over-explores there. What this arm also shows is that this local improvement is too small to steer the endpoint. Stalled batches are only about a fifth of the budget, and the extra stalled-batch gain (about +0.04 summed over 13 sessions) is far smaller than the variation between runs that diverge after the first stall: single cells move by 0.10 to 0.13 depending on whether a session breaks out of a stall early or stays stuck. Raw stalled-batch totals do not discriminate between the two directions, since both widening and contraction raised them while both lost on the panel. Per-pick quality does discriminate: mean offspring score, parent-beating rate and same-pool swap quality. Future arms on stall-time allocation should be judged on those, not on totals that grow or shrink with exposure. Two leads remain open, and neither can be settled from one realization. First, the Child's ordinary batches after a stall realized less gain than the Parent's. That may be path noise, or it may mean contraction narrows what the population later breeds from: the molecular review found the Child's top zaleplon molecules collapsed onto 8 skeletons against the Parent's 16, sitting on a flat plateau of halogen swaps. Second, a constant contraction neither escalates nor lets go without an improvement. One sitagliptin session stayed contracted for its last 14 batches and finished 0.10 below the Parent, which is the case TuRBO handles with a restart this arm did not adopt. The route on this knob should stop here. Both directions are measured at the bound trigger, removal is already known to cost about 0.12, and any further dose would be a sweep. If stall-time behaviour is pursued further, the lever is what happens once a stall ends, or the plateau-forming edits of the generator, not the amplitude of the stalled-batch draw. Placing this delta against this round's neutral path-divergence reference is left to Curate.
finding_summary.results: The change ran exactly as registered. Every session was identical to the Parent until its first stalled batch, the two deco_hop sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent record for record, the sampled deviation was exactly two thirds of the Parent's in stalled batches and untouched everywhere else, and the logged stall counter matched an independent recount in all 435 batches. Inside stalled batches the allocator did what the contraction was meant to do. On the 13 identical first-stall pools it changed 54 of 130 picks and swapped in 38 molecules, moving the average pick from the 78th to the 88th percentile of predicted score and cutting tiny fragment picks from 6 to 3, exactly the preregistered numbers. Across all of its own stalled batches, picks sat at the 91st percentile of predicted score (Parent 84th), with fewer picks from the model's uncertain tail (15 against 43) and fewer fragments (12 against 22). The swapped-in molecules were better bets: on identical pools they averaged 0.473 against 0.350 for the molecules the Parent evaluated instead, higher in 12 of 13 sessions, which is the mirror image of the earlier widening arm (0.18 against 0.36). Stalls ended sooner: a third of stalled batches broke the stall (27.5% for the Parent) and resolved stalls lasted 2.1 batches instead of 3.2, so the Child spent 79 batches stalled instead of 91. Within those batches offspring beat their parents more often (10.9% against 8.6%), positive parent-relative gain rose from 1.64 to 1.89 and summed incumbent improvement from 0.477 to 0.519, but the number of incumbent improvements stayed at 28 and the mean offspring score stayed at 0.405. The gain was not broad: stalled-batch improvement was higher in only 5 of 13 sessions, and much of the first-stall advantage came from one sitagliptin session. None of this reached the endpoint. After the first stall the Child's ordinary batches realized less than the Parent's (0.470 against 0.563 summed incumbent gain, lower in 8 of 13 sessions), so total gain after the trigger was 0.989 against 1.039. The complete 15-cell mean fell 0.0033 (0.5931 against 0.5965), short of the +0.002 bar, with seeds at -0.029, +0.020 and -0.001. Two sitagliptin cells swung -0.103 and +0.129, and dropping any single cell moves the mean anywhere from -0.013 to +0.004. The loss is inside the -0.014 to +0.008 spread of the earlier same-trigger arms.

molecular.headline: Ordinary-sized fused aromatic heterocycles decorated with N-halogen, O-halogen, nitroso and strained small rings
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task (4,350 total, 873-879 unique per task) of entirely ordinary size and ring content: mean SMILES length 42-58 characters, 24-32 heavy atoms, 3-5 ring bonds, and per the digest counters 97-98% of proposals carry a ring closure and 96-97% carry an aromatic atom. The skeletons are recognisable medicinal-chemistry cores - indole-2-carboxamides, quinolines, xanthine/purine-like diazine-diones, piperazine-2,5-dione polycycles, chlorophenyl-alkyl-amines - so the problem is not the scaffold but the decoration. The decoration layer is where the chemistry fails: 700 of 4,350 proposals carry a nitrogen-halogen bond, 203 an oxygen-halogen bond, 241 a nitroso group, 432 a thiocarbonyl; a string parse finds a 3- or 4-membered ring in 5-37% of each set, frequently on atoms written as aromatic. The digest counters also show stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0 in every set: not one of the 4,350 molecules specifies a stereocentre or a charge, although the leaders contain several sp3 stereocentres each. 99 proposals have 4 or fewer heavy atoms. Halogenation is always single-atom: zero trifluoromethyl groups in 4,350 molecules. context.comparison reports the Child complete on three seeds and completely paired against code Parent n-1744a1494180 (paired_mean_delta -0.003338); all 15 Child staging trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were present and read. The two molecule sets are chemically near-identical - on one objective the Child's seed-0 best molecule is the same SMILES at the same evaluation index as the Parent's - with one visible difference: the Child's highest band on one objective collapses onto fewer halogen-masked skeletons than the Parent's (8 versus 16 over the top 30).

per_task.generated_character: The smallest set: mean 24.2 heavy atoms, 3 ring bonds, nothing above 39 heavy atoms. One chemotype dominates - a methoxy/alkyl-substituted indole or 7-azaindole bearing a C2 carboxamide, thioamide, glyoxamide or ester to a pyridin-3-yl or phenyl ring - clearly grown from the initial pool's indole-2-carboxamide COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC (0.3051). 318 of 870 keep an [nH] indole NH, 432 carry a C(=O)N amide group, 183 a thiocarbonyl, 747 at least one halogen and 317 a nitrogen-halogen bond. 23 proposals are sub-fragments of 4 or fewer heavy atoms.
liabilities: an N-bromo or N-fluoro pyridinyl amide in all 12 digest best molecules, e.g. CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)N(Br)c1cccnc1)n2F - these are oxidants, not isolable amides
halogenation of the azole ring nitrogen (n2F, n2Br, n2Cl) in the entire top band; 317 of 870 carry an N-halogen bond
thioamides and thioesters in 183 of 870, e.g. COc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=S)Cc3ccccn3)n2Br)c1OC (0.4047)
an S-N-S aminothio chain on a final-batch molecule, CC1Cc2c(NSN)cc3[nH]c(C(=O)Oc4cccnc4)cc3c21 (0.3154)
23 of 870 evaluations spent on sub-fragments, including the 1,2-dioxetane C1COO1 and SCl, all scoring 0.0
a 69-of-870 incidence of 4-membered rings fused into the aromatic core
missing_features: an aromatic nitrile: 1 of 870 proposals contains C#N
a fused five-membered aromatic N-N ring of the pyrazolo type: 10 of 870 contain an aromatic n-n
a tertiary N-acyl-N-alkyl aniline on a carbon-only benzo scaffold; the amide here is always hung off the azole C2

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises 0.3051 -> 0.4447 by alkylating the benzo ring, keeping the C2 amide, and swapping the anilide for a pyridin-3-yl amide: pairs identical except phenyl/pyridyl differ 0.4399 versus 0.4447. Above that the gradient is flat in exactly the dimension the search edited - nine digest best molecules sit at exactly 0.4447 differing only in which of F/Cl/Br sits on the amide nitrogen and the ring nitrogen, and the top 50 proposals show only 11 distinct scores with a 10-molecule plateau. Halogen-free proposals reach 0.4397 against 0.4447 for the 747 halogenated ones, so halogenation bought about 0.005 while occupying 86% of the set.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and most heavily fused set: mean 31.5 heavy atoms, mean 4.2 ring bonds, 50 proposals at 45 or more heavy atoms and a maximum of 96. Two chemotypes. One session reaches a purine-like tricyclic - a pyrazolo-fused pyrimidinedione-thione carrying a pendant 4-aryl pyrimidine-fused ring - at 0.8338-0.8561. The other two plateau at 0.60-0.64 on a hexasubstituted benzene bearing a nitroso-substituted aminomethine and a four-membered ring fused to a second arene, or on an oxazinone-fused biaryl with nitriles. 245 of 870 carry a nitrile, 240 a nitroso group, 207 a thione, 63 an O-halogen bond, and only 15 an ordinary amide.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The set has a hard floor at 0.5: the six worst digest molecules are single atoms and tiny fragments (Cl, F, C=C, N=O, BrSBr, BrCOBr) and all score exactly 0.5, as do the initial pool members (0.5000-0.5484). Everything the search earns comes from assembling a fused bi/tricyclic diazine-dione plus a nitrogen-rich pendant aryl; the 0.8561 band appears in one session only, and its three members differ only in C(F)OCCl versus C(F)F and Cl versus CCl, so the top is again flat in decoration. The two sessions that never build that tricyclic core stop at 0.6442 with nitroso aromatics.

per_task.generated_character: The widest score range of the five (0.00017 to 0.9956) over molecules of mean 30.5 heavy atoms. Its lowest-scoring proposals descend from the initial pool's aryl sulfonamide and amino-acid-like fragments; the leaders are lipophilic amines: a 1,3-disubstituted benzene bearing Br/Cl/ethynyl, a two-carbon tether, a basic secondary or tertiary nitrogen in either an acyclic 1,4-diaminobutane chain or a 1,4-diazepane, and a second 3-chlorophenyl on the carbon next to that nitrogen. 857 of 870 carry a halogen, 400 an N-alkyl amine token, 150 a 1,4-diaminobutane chain or 1,4-diazepane ring, only 8 an amide and 46 a carboxylic acid. The sulfonyl group inherited from the initial pool survives in 73 proposals, none later than evaluation 47.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The climb from 0.0002 to 0.99 is one clean pharmacophore assembly: the worst molecules are the inherited dichlorobenzenesulfonyl-pyrrolidine amides (CC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1, 0.0002); dropping the sulfonamide and the acid and installing a protonatable amine two carbons from a halogenated arene with a second aryl already reaches 0.7417 at the set median. Above 0.99 only decoration moves - Cl to Br, methyl to ethyl, amine in a ring or on a chain - spreading the 12 best over 0.0035. The 13 halogen-free proposals average 0.0748 against 0.5955 for the 857 halogenated ones, so lipophilic halogenated aryl is the single most rewarded feature here.

per_task.generated_character: The most nearly drug-like set and the lowest-scoring one: mean 30.6 heavy atoms, mean 4.4 ring bonds, and almost halogen-free (only 92 of 870 carry a halogen, against 690-857 on the other four objectives). Chemistry is dominated by cyclic ureas and imides - 528 of 870 contain an N-C(=O)-N dione and 706 an N-alkyl nitrogen token, most of which is the N-methyl or N-ethyl of that imide or urea rather than a basic amine - fused to an alkoxy-aryl. Two families recur: a bridged ethoxy-benzo plus benzodioxole (112 of 870 contain the OCO group) carrying a 1,3-dialkyl piperazine-2,5-dione, reaching 0.2359; and a 2-propylquinoline attached to a methylated bicyclic dione, around 0.21. Only 11 proposals are sub-fragments, the fewest of the five sets.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score runs 0.0183 (initial) to 0.2359 and the whole gradient is chemotype assembly: combine an alkoxy-arene, a second oxygenated arene and a dialkylated cyclic imide/urea into one fused polycycle. Beyond that the surface is nearly flat - the top 50 proposals span 0.236 to about 0.218 across 42 distinct scores and 30 distinct halogen-masked skeletons, so large skeletal rearrangements barely move the score and no decoration pushes past 0.236. Halogenated and halogen-free proposals score the same here (0.1814 versus 0.1854 mean), the only objective where halogen is neutral.

per_task.generated_character: Compact and heavily fluorinated: mean 25.9 heavy atoms, mean 3.7 ring bonds, nothing above 45 heavy atoms. 774 of 870 carry a halogen, 359 carry three or more fluorines and the maximum is five F in one molecule. The chemotype is a xanthine/purine-like pyrimidinedione fused to a pyrrole, bearing N-CH2F and N-CH2CH2F chains, an exocyclic imine (385 of 870 contain a (=N) group) and an N-linked cyclopentenol or methoxy-fluorophenyl. 323 of 870 carry a nitrogen-halogen bond and 73 contain a three-membered ring. 24 proposals are bare atoms or two-atom fragments.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Fluorine is the whole gradient: the 96 halogen-free proposals average 0.0372 and peak at 0.3088, while the 774 halogenated ones average 0.2329 and reach 0.6286; within the top band score tracks the count and placement of F (0.5950-0.6286 differ by one CH2F or CF2 position on the same core). The gradient is also unusually brittle at the end of the run: the two last final-batch molecules keep one scaffold and differ only in the N-chain, a 3-fluoropropyl at 0.5264 against a chlorohydrin CC(O)Cl at 0.0381, so the surface rewards specifically fluorine, not any halogen.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 0 of the 4,350 optimizer proposals across all five objectives contain a trifluoromethyl group, although on one objective 774 of 870 molecules carry fluorine, its best molecule carries five separate F atoms (Cn1c(=O)n(NCF)c(=O)c2c(C3CC(F)C3(F)F)n(C3=CC(F)C=C3O)cc21, 0.6286) and only 39 proposals there contain even a gem-difluoro pair. Halogen-bearing proposals outscore halogen-free ones there 0.2329 to 0.0372 on average, so the search is clearly trying to fluorinate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen enters only as a single atom; no multi-atom halogenated substituent is ever assembled.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom substitution cannot reach any group that needs three identical atoms on one carbon, because every intermediate must be separately accepted. Add group-level insertion that places whole standard substituents (fully halogenated methyl, nitro, cyano, acetyl, sulfonyl) as one edit from a fixed fragment table, so one accepted move yields the finished group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 700 of 4,350 proposals contain a nitrogen-halogen bond and 203 an oxygen-halogen bond. On one objective all 12 of the digest's best molecules carry both an N-bromo/N-fluoro amide and a halogenated ring nitrogen (CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)N(Br)c1cccnc1)n2F, 0.4447), and 317 of its 870 proposals carry such a bond. On another, 8 of the 12 best carry an aryl hypofluorite (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3, 0.8561). The generator's single highest-scoring region on two objectives therefore rests on bonds no chemist can make.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen and heteroatom substitution is applied to nitrogen and oxygen positions that cannot carry it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substitution operator treats every hydrogen-bearing position as interchangeable. It needs an environment-aware target filter that admits halogen only on carbon and rejects products containing N-X or O-X single bonds, so the surrogate and the population are not trained on an unmakeable sub-space.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 74 of 4,350 proposals contain a sulfonyl group. All of them occur at or before evaluation 47 and only in the two sessions whose initial pool already supplied one (CC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1); none appears later in any of the 15 sessions. Yet polar linkers are clearly viable when present: 432 of 870 proposals on one objective are amides and 528 of 870 on another are cyclic ureas.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-oxidation-state sulfur and other polar linkers can only be inherited, never created.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: No operator changes a heteroatom's oxidation state or swaps one polar linker for another as a unit, so a group lost when the parent pool turns over is unreachable for the rest of the run. A whole-linker replacement move that interconverts amide, sulfonamide, sulfone, ester and urea on the same attachment points would restore that axis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A string parse of all 4,350 proposals finds a 4-membered ring in 69, 188, 230, 144 and 322 of the 870 molecules per objective, and a 3-membered ring in up to 73; between 5% and 21% per objective put such a ring on atoms written as aromatic. They sit in the leaders, not only the tail: N=c1c2c(F)n(C3(CF)C(O)=CC=C3CCF)c3c2n-3c(=O)n1CCF (0.6166) and COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2 (0.6442). The published Parent n-1744a1494180 shows the same defect class at comparable rates on the same panel (190 and 254 of its 870 proposals on two objectives), so this is a standing property of the generator rather than a new effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits create three- and four-membered rings fused into aromatic systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring bonds are chosen by attachment index with no check on the ring that results. Constrain new ring closures to 5-, 6- and 7-membered products and forbid any closure that creates a 3- or 4-membered ring sharing two atoms with an aromatic ring, while still offering a valid larger-ring alternative so the edit is not simply lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0 for all five proposal sets, i.e. none of 4,350 molecules carries a stereo descriptor or a formal charge, although the leading molecules contain several sp3 stereocentres each: the ring-fusion carbons of CCOc1ccc2c3c1CC1CN(C)C(=O)N(CC)C(=O)CCC(c4ccccc4OCO2)N31 (0.2359) and the substituted benzylic carbon of C#Cc1cc(Br)cc(CCN2CCCCNC2(CC)c2cccc(Cl)c2)c1 (0.9956).
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemistry and ionization state are never expressed at all.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and every operator are stereo-blind and charge-blind, so a configurationally defined or ionization-dependent target can only ever be approached as an unspecified mixture. Either carry stereo descriptors through crossover and mutation with an explicit set/invert move, or record the omission as a representation boundary so it is not mistaken for a search failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective the best molecule places two ring nitrogens on a single carbon that also bears an aryl and an ethyl (C#Cc1cc(Br)cc(CCN2CCCCNC2(CC)c2cccc(Cl)c2)c1, 0.9956), a near-best adds a thio-aminal (CCC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)NCCCCN1CCc1cc(C(N)S)cc(Br)c1C, 0.9928), and 0 of that objective's top 50 molecules contain a plain piperazine- or piperidine-type ring. The same pattern recurs elsewhere as an N-N ring-fusion node in CCOc1ccc2c3c1CC1CN(C)C(=O)N(CC)C(=O)CCC(c4ccccc4OCO2)N31 (0.2359), an N-S sulfenamide on imide nitrogen in CCOC(=O)c1cccc(N2C(c3ccccc3)=C3C(=O)N(S)C(=O)N(C)C32)c1 (0.1602) and an S-N-S chain in CC1Cc2c(NSN)cc3[nH]c(C(=O)Oc4cccnc4)cc3c21 (0.3154).
transferable_gaps.gap: Heteroatoms pile onto one sp3 carbon or bond directly to each other, instead of being carried on stable rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Substitution is accepted on atoms already bonded to a heteroatom, which turns a correct pharmacophore into a hydrolytically hopeless one. Add a neighbourhood rule that blocks a second heteroatom on an sp3 carbon already bearing one and blocks new heteroatom-heteroatom single bonds, and provide saturated nitrogen-heterocycle fragments as insertable units so a basic nitrogen can be introduced on a stable ring instead.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 99 of 4,350 proposals have 4 or fewer heavy atoms (bare C, F, O, Cl, FF, SCl, C1COO1) and all sit at or near the floor of their set. On one objective nine digest best molecules share exactly the score 0.4447 and differ only in which of F/Cl/Br sits on the amide and ring nitrogens; its top 50 proposals carry only 11 distinct scores with a 10-molecule plateau, and its top 30 collapse to 8 distinct skeletons once halogens are masked, against 16 for the published Parent n-1744a1494180 on the same panel.
transferable_gaps.gap: Evaluations are spent on edits that cannot change the objective value: halogen permutations and sub-fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Novelty is measured by canonical string identity, which a halogen swap always defeats, and there is no lower bound on candidate size. A minimum heavy-atom precondition plus a duplicate test that treats halogen-only differences at the same position as the same candidate would return those evaluations to the search without touching the operators.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 31 of 4,350 proposals contain a repeated 14-character substring and they measure far below their own set's mean (0.0515 against 0.5877 on one objective, 0.0130 against 0.2113 on another). The largest proposals reach 86 and 96 heavy atoms this way, e.g. the two duplicated dichlorobenzenesulfonyl-pyrrolidine blocks of COc1cc(F)cc(C=CC=C(CC(C(=O)C2CCCN2S(=O)(=O)c2cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c2)C2C=CC(c3cc(F)cc(OC)c3)=CCC2)C(=O)CC(NC(=O)C2CCCN2S(=O)(=O)c2cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c2)C2=CC(c3cc(F)cc(OC)c3)C=C2)c1 (0.0289), while on another objective 50 proposals exceed 45 heavy atoms, the largest reaching 96 by carrying four copies of the same pyrimidinedione block at 0.5628.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecules grow by appending a copy of a fragment already present rather than by editing substituents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Fragment recombination joins two parents with no size or self-similarity control, so a share of the budget goes to dimer-like adducts that are guaranteed to measure below both parents. Bound the product's heavy-atom count relative to its parents and reject products whose added fragment duplicates a fragment already in the molecule.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local accepted-only chronological archive; greedy-64 score/serial survivors; score-quantile parent sampling (edges 0.1/0.25/0.5, weights 0.6/0.3/0.1); bounded fresh-pool refill at multiplier 16 (160 candidates per announced batch of ten, attempt limit 50,000).

All seven graph mutation operator families with unchanged weights; connected-fragment crossover at 0.45 with optional post-crossover mutation 0.35; ordinary mutation continuation; disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange.
Stable canonical/isomeric identity admission and both duplicate scopes (emitted-or-initial and temporary pool).
Maximum-per-signature sulfur admission over the ORIGINAL scored generating parents with its neutral envelope and rejection bookkeeping.

Accepted-only radius-two chirality-aware 2048-bin integer Morgan-count GP with generalized dot-product Tanimoto kernel, raw mean and population-SD normalization with 0.001 floor, noise SD 0.05, float64 covariance and Cholesky with the original jitter ladder, finite guards and fallback routing.

Correlated Thompson fresh-pool allocation (m-000000000006 sampled residual influence, m-000000000007 cross-candidate correlation) with the exact single standard-normal array draw, sequential availability masks and first-index ties; prospective prediction and feedback diagnostics.

NEW: stall-conditioned residual contraction. A session-local counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches (reset on a strictly improving batch) multiplies only the sampled residual by 0.6666666666666666 while the counter is at least 3, factor exactly 1.0 otherwise, plus passive same-pool replay diagnostics that consume no random numbers and route no choice.
